test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 30 Sept 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: In a room, a magnetic field is applied vertically upwards. Electron and proton beams are released horizontally from south towards the north direction into this field. The directions of deflections of these beams will be ______ and ______, respectively.
solution:
The correct answer is __**west, east**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A magnetic field applied vertically upwards with electron and proton beams entering horizontally from south to north will interact according to the right-hand rule for moving charges in a magnetic field.
 
• **Electrons**, having a negative charge, will **deflect towards the left (west)** due to the magnetic Lorentz force acting perpendicular to their motion.
 
• **Protons**, being positively charged, will **deflect towards the right (east)** as they experience a force in the opposite direction to that of electrons.
 
• Therefore, the directions of deflections of the electron and proton beams will be west and east, respectively.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lorentz Force: **The force exerted on a charged particle moving through a magnetic field, given by (F=q(vtimes B)) ), where ( q ) is the charge, ( v ) is the velocity, and ( B ) is the magnetic field.
 
• **Right-Hand Rule:** A mnemonic for predicting the direction of the Lorentz force; for a positively charged particle, point the thumb of the right hand in the direction of velocity, fingers in the direction of the magnetic field, and the force on the particle comes out of the palm.
 
• Magnetic Field Influence: The magnetic field does not do work on a particle; it alters the direction of motion but not the speed (kinetic energy remains constant).
 
• Charged Particle Motion: In a magnetic field, charged particles can move in circular or helical paths depending on their initial velocity relative to the direction of the magnetic field.
